requirements.statement: In each select element, each optgroup element has a label attribute.

citations.quote: Dans chaque balise `<select>`, chaque balise `<optgroup>` possède-t-elle un attribut `label` ?
Pour chaque élément `<optgroup>`, vérifier qu’il possède un attribut `label` ;

routes.statement: The optgroup element carries a label attribute.

rationale.text: The test asks one thing of each optgroup element in a select: that it has a label attribute. It names one way to meet it and gives no exception, and the criterion has no particular case. Whether an element carries an attribute is a fact of the DOM, so a custom check can decide it. Whether the attribute's content is relevant is test 11.8.3, so here an empty label attribute meets the test: the element has the attribute. The check looks at every optgroup with a select ancestor, in every document and shadow tree of the page. It abstains by stated rules on the cases this test's text leaves open. A list outside any form: the criterion is asked of each form, and the glossary defines a form as a form element or an element with role form. A list that is not rendered, not exposed to assistive technologies, or invisible: the test gives no exception for hidden lists, but whether a native list hidden behind a scripted replacement is one it covers is open. An optgroup that is not a child of its select, or that is itself hidden. An optgroup with a legend child, a labelling form that the HTML standard added after RGAA 4.1.2 and that the text does not consider. On every other optgroup it decides: no fault when the label attribute is present, fault when it is absent. A fault on such an optgroup means the requirement is violated, since the one route is missing and there is no exception, so the link's fault means failure; it covers the one route for every optgroup the test applies to, so it is resolving and the candidate is full. The route can pass: a visible list in a form whose optgroups all carry a label attribute gets no_fault. The cost of the abstentions is that a page with such lists gets needs review instead of a result. No axe-core rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is structural: the test applies to optgroup elements in a select, which code finds with certainty, and a page holding none is not applicable. Needs is empty: the lists are read on the page as loaded.

citations.quote: Dans chaque balise `<select>`, chaque balise `<optgroup>` possède-t-elle un attribut `label` ?
Balise <form> ou balise possédant un attribut WAI-ARIA role="form".
Si c’est le cas pour chaque élément `<optgroup>`, **le test est validé**.
